label: sec:hoefsmit-convergence-magic-shells-preamble
html:
In the Wedderburn decomposition of H_A(q) at the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the three-row antisymmetric weight y_{(1^3)} vanishes identically, forcing the ordinary Markov trace to factor through the two-row Temperley–Lieb quotient \mathrm{TL}_A(q). This section traces the physical and cohomological consequences of that two-row concentration across four stages:

  1. The ^4\mathrm{He} channel and magic-A binding: On the active two-row stratum \lambda = (A-k, k), Frobenius norm minimization collapses the \beta-transition operator to a scalar multiple of the identity, T_\beta = S\cdot\mathbf{1}, isolating the magic-A binding formula and the Bring residue resolvent.
  2. The binding generating function and jet-degree filtration: Identifying bond order with jet filtration degree turns the many-body binding expansion into a q-difference equation whose period involution statistic exhibits palindromic symmetry.
  3. q-difference prolongation and conserved periods: Prolonging the q-difference kernel across fixed depth yields an \mathfrak{sl}_2 recurrence with an explicit Wronskian conserved quantity.
  4. Substrate cohomology calibration: Aligning the prolonged periods with the three cohomology calibration anchors (m_e, q_0, m_\pi) splits every observable into bar-even (\cosh) binding components and bar-odd (\sinh) decay components, while the Wenzl A-operator and one-dimensional Hecke characters provide closed-form boundary evaluations.
